input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 gives only cause-based, insolvency and Customer cause-like triggers (9.1-9.3), and Section 27.3 a force-majeure exit; there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and Section 2.1 expressly denies termination rights across a three-year committed term (Section 8.1). That is walk-away territory under T4C (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term), so it fails the fallback, and 30 days' notice cannot rest on the fallback band of 60-90 days. Section 10.2 refunds only prepaid *recurring* Fees for the period after termination, which is neither an express pro-rata refund nor a refund of prepaid non-recurring Fees, so the refund element is carried in the new clause. Vendor has no convenience right, which is favourable to us; we state that expressly rather than leaving it to inference. New Section 9.4 sits between 9.3 and 9.5 so the conforming cross-reference in Section 2.1 resolves, and the no-reduction restriction in 2.1 is preserved.

proposal.summary: Add Customer 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees, bar Vendor convenience termination, and conform take-or-pay clause
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a convenience exit: we have added a Customer right to terminate on thirty days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and confirmed Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term. We also conformed the take-or-pay sentence in Section 2.1, which otherwise denies us any termination right, while leaving the no-reduction restriction intact.

ops.oldText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction rights but subject to Section 9.4.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
